topics.name: Using phrases: relieved of, likened to, escort, draw the curtain
Polite requests and offers (May I, Could you, I would like to)

options: The Principal gave she a book.
The Principal gave her a book.
The Principal gave to her a book.
questions.rule: The indirect object comes first without 'to', in object form: gave her (indirect) a book (direct).

options: May I requesting you to switch off your mobiles?
May I requested you to switch off your mobiles?
May I request you to switch off your mobiles?
questions.rule: After May I, use the base verb: May I request ...?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: lit
lighting
lights

questions.rule: Passive = was + past participle: light - lit - lit.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: their
them
theirs

questions.rule: An object pronoun is needed after the verb: give them a round of applause.

questions.before: After the medicine, Ravi was relieved
options: at
with
of
questions.rule: The phrase is to be relieved of something (pain, worry, a duty).

questions.after: I request you all to be seated?
options: May
Am
Have
questions.rule: A polite request to do something: May I + base verb?
Verb + indirect object (us) + direct object (her new painting).

options: May I having a glass of water, please?
May I has a glass of water, please?
May I have a glass of water, please?
questions.rule: May I + base verb: May I have ...?

options: The prize was won by Zubin.
The prize was win by Zubin.
The prize were won by Zubin.
questions.rule: Passive: was + past participle: win - won - won. 'Prize' is singular, so was.

questions.source: The Chief Guest gave Anagha a prize.
options: The Chief Guest gave a prize for Anagha.
The Chief Guest gave to Anagha a prize.
The Chief Guest gave a prize to Anagha.
questions.rule: Put the direct object first and the person after to: gave a prize to Anagha.

options: The guests was welcomed with books.
The guests were welcomes with books.
The guests were welcomed with books.
questions.rule: Plural subject (guests) + were + past participle: were welcomed.

options: The minister was escort by his bodyguards.
The minister was escorted from his bodyguards.
The minister was escorted by his bodyguards.
questions.rule: Passive: was escorted by (the doer comes after by).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: our
us
ours

questions.rule: The indirect object must be an object pronoun: taught us a new style.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: helping
help
helped

questions.rule: After Could you, use the base verb: Could you please help ...?

options: they
them
their
questions.rule: Indirect object = object pronoun: sang them a song.

options: given
gave
give
questions.rule: Future passive = will be + past participle: will be given.
Could you please + base verb ...? is a polite request.

options: He gave me a book of stories.
He gave I a book of stories.
He gave to me a book of stories.
questions.rule: Indirect object (me) + direct object (a book), with no 'to' in between.

questions.source: The Head Girl escorted the guests.
options: The guests were escorted by the Head Girl.
The guests are escorted by the Head Girl.
The guests was escorted by the Head Girl.
questions.rule: Simple past active -> were + past participle for a plural subject: were escorted.

questions.prompt: Change into a polite request beginning with 'Could'.
options: Could you please open the window?
Could you please opens the window?
Could you please opened the window?
questions.rule: Could you please + base verb, and end with ?

options: The teacher bought they some paint.
The teacher bought the children some paint.
The teacher bought some paint the children.
questions.rule: Without 'for', the indirect object comes first: bought the children (indirect) some paint (direct).

options: Knowledge is likened with a lamp.
Knowledge is liken to a lamp.
Knowledge is likened to a lamp.
questions.rule: The phrase is to be likened to something (compared to it).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: escorted
escorting
escorts

questions.rule: Passive = were + past participle: were escorted.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: enjoying
enjoyed
enjoys

questions.rule: Passive = was + past participle: was enjoyed.

questions.after: our Principal to address the audience.
options: to request
requesting
request
questions.rule: would like is followed by to + verb: I would like to request ...
Verb + indirect object (Anagha) + direct object (a medal).
Passive: was sung (sing - sang - sung) + by + the doer.

chat: Excuse me, where should I sit?
options: Please takes a seat in the front row.
Please take a seat in the front row.
Please taking a seat in the front row.
questions.rule: A polite instruction: Please + base verb: Please take a seat.

chat: How did you feel just before the results?
options: I had butterflies in my stomach.
I had butterflies in mine stomach.
I was having butterflies in my stomachs.
questions.rule: The phrase is to have butterflies in my stomach - 'my' before a noun, and one stomach.

options: Mother made some laddoos for we.
Mother made some laddoos to us.
Mother made some laddoos for us.
questions.rule: Direct object first, then for + object pronoun: some laddoos for us.

options: The paintings has been displayed in the hall.
The paintings have been display in the hall.
The paintings have been displayed in the hall.
questions.rule: Present perfect passive: have been + past participle; 'paintings' is plural, so have.

questions.prompt: Pick the correct suggestion with a question tag.
options: Let's start the programme, shall we?
Let's start the programme, will we?
Let's starts the programme, shall we?
questions.rule: Let's + base verb, and the tag is always shall we?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: myself
me
mine

questions.rule: Both people are the indirect object, so use the object form: my brother and me.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: gave
given
giving

questions.rule: Passive = was + past participle: give - gave - given.

questions.after: curtain, let us stand for the National Anthem.
options: an
these
the
questions.rule: The phrase is to draw the curtain (to end the programme).

questions.before: Thank you for inviting my parents and
options: I
mine
me
questions.rule: After 'inviting', both people are objects, so use me: my parents and me.
A polite offer: Would you like to + base verb ...?

options: Yes, it has decorated with flowers.
Yes, it has been decorated with flowers.
Yes, it have been decorated with flowers.
questions.rule: Present perfect passive: has been + past participle: it has been decorated.

questions.source: The compere said to the audience, "Please take your seats."
options: The compere requested the audience to took their seats.
The compere requested the audience take your seats.
The compere requested the audience to take their seats.
questions.rule: A polite command becomes requested + person + to + base verb; 'your' becomes their.

questions.source: The prizes were given away by the Chief Guest.
options: The Chief Guest gave away the prizes.
The Chief Guest gives away the prizes.
The Chief Guest given away the prizes.
questions.rule: The doer becomes the subject; 'were given' is past, so use gave away.

options: Our principal handed each of us a certificate.
Our principal handed each of we a certificate.
Our principal handed each of us certificate.
questions.rule: Indirect object each of us (object form) + direct object a certificate (with its article).

options: The winners will be announced after the play.
The winners will announced after the play.
The winners will be announce after the play.
questions.rule: Future passive: will be + past participle: will be announced.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: requested
request
requests

questions.rule: would like to + base verb: I would like to request ...

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: giving
gives
given

questions.rule: Passive = was + past participle: was given.

questions.after: all the very best for the exams.
options: we
us
our
questions.rule: The indirect object is an object pronoun: wished us all the very best.
Future passive with two objects: will be given + their prizes.

questions.source: Mrs Joshi taught our class a new song.
options: Mrs Joshi teached a new song to our class.
Mrs Joshi taught a new songs to our class.
Mrs Joshi taught a new song to our class.
questions.rule: Direct object first, then to + indirect object: taught a new song to our class.

chat: Shall I make some tea for your friends?
options: Yes, please. That will being very kind of you.
Yes, please. That would be very kindly of you.
Yes, please. That would be very kind of you.
questions.rule: Accept an offer with That would be very kind of you - would + be + adjective.

chat: Did you send Mr Rao our team photos?
options: Yes, I sent he the photos this morning.
Yes, I sent him the photos this morning.
Yes, I send him the photos this morning.
questions.rule: Past (sent) + indirect object pronoun (him) + direct object (the photos).

questions.source: The Chief Guest will release the book.
options: The book will be released by the Chief Guest.
The book will released by the Chief Guest.
The book would be release by the Chief Guest.
questions.rule: Future active -> will be + past participle: will be released.
